clinician.trajectory_summary: A 13-year-old girl presented with headaches beginning at age 7 and right-sided weakness (power 4/5) with sensory deficits, brisk reflexes, and minimal facial asymmetry. Initial head CT (E001) revealed a left parieto-temporal infarct with cerebral atrophy. One year after initial presentation, she developed new-onset complex partial seizures characterized by mumbling, blank stare, and drowsiness (E003), and was initiated on sodium valproate 200 mg twice daily. Follow-up MRI (E004) demonstrated universal atrophy of the left cerebral hemisphere with ventricular enlargement, ipsilateral calvarial thickening, and hyperpneumatization of the left frontal sinus—findings pathognomonic for DDMS secondary to early cerebral insult.
